name: Ly Cong Uan
role: Điện tiền chỉ huy sứ under the Tiền Lê, then founding emperor who moved the capital from Hoa Lư to Thăng Long
known_facts: Commander of the capital guard (điện tiền chỉ huy sứ) at Hoa Lư under Lê Long Đĩnh
Ascended the throne in November 1009 with the support of Đào Cam Mộc and thiền sư Vạn Hạnh, era name Thuận Thiên
Moved the capital from Hoa Lư to Đại La, renamed it Thăng Long
Divided the country into 24 lộ, remitted taxes for three years, collected only four of six tax kinds
Four personal campaigns plus four dispatched expeditions against local revolts and a Chiêm Thành raid
Sent envoys to fetch the Đại Tạng kinh from the Song in 1018; promoted Buddhism as state ideology
Died 1028 after a 19-year reign, temple name Lý Thái Tổ
interpretation: Early-Lý imperial and military dress based on the user reference.
unknowns: No verified contemporary life portrait survives
